T5 is done. `out/T5/` holds the merged sharded checkpoint plus `solution.py`, `run.sh`, and `REPORT.md`.

**Approach.** I checked the base key set before picking a route, and that ruled out the obvious condition-F path. The base checkpoint stores 48 tensors that `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` treats as non-persistent buffers (`attention.bias` as U8 `[1,1,2048,2048]`, `attention.masked_bias`, `rotary_emb.inv_freq`). `peft.merge_and_unload` + `save_pretrained` would have dropped all of them and emitted ~196 tensors instead of the required 244. So I worked directly on the tensor files with `safetensors` + `torch`, and sharded with `huggingface_hub.split_torch_state_dict_into_shards` — the same splitter `save_pretrained` uses — so the shard naming and index schema follow the standard convention.

**Result** (verified independently afterwards, in float64, against the raw inputs):
- 16 adapter pairs merged, `scale = alpha/r = 2`, `W += 2 * B @ A` in float32 then cast back to float16; worst relative Frobenius error **2.076e-04** against the 1e-3 limit.
- 244 tensors, key set identical to the base, no `lora_` names; the 228 untouched tensors are bit-identical to the input.
- 4 shards at 505.1 / 500.3 / 500.3 / 488.2 MiB of tensor data, all under the 512 MiB budget, plus `model.safetensors.index.json` mapping all 244 names.

The run enforces the four required checks (plus rank/layout/shape guards and a bit-exactness audit) before writing, and re-reads the written checkpoint afterwards to confirm it.

Two things worth flagging:

- **The task text is wrong about the embeddings.** It says `gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` and `embed_out.weight` at "206 MB each" are larger than the 512 MiB budget and must sit alone. 206 MB is 196.5 MiB — comfortably under 536,870,912 bytes — so that clause is vacuous here and greedy packing puts them in shards with other tensors.
